c.tagline: India's Garden City turned tech capital — craft beer, startups, and near-perfect weather.

taxi.fareNote: Yellow-and-black or yellow-green auto-rickshaws are the workhorse of local travel; insist on the meter or book via app, as fixed 'no-meter' quotes to tourists run high. City taxis are almost always booked through Uber or Ola rather than hailed on the street.

emergency.note: 112 is India's single all-services emergency number; 108 is the dedicated ambulance line, 100 reaches police and 101 fire.

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets in the KR Market and Majestic bus-stand crowds, insist auto-rickshaw drivers use the meter, and women should avoid empty streets late at night.

hood_desc: The colonial-era heart of the city around MG Road, Brigade Road, and Church Street, with shopping, restaurants, Cubbon Park, and Vidhana Soudha nearby; best for first-timers who want a walkable central base on the metro Purple Line.

Bengaluru's trendiest district, where 100 Feet Road and 12th Main are packed with craft-beer pubs, rooftop bars, boutiques, and cafes; suits travelers who want upscale nightlife and dining, well-connected by metro.

A buzzing startup and cafe hub full of young professionals, breweries, restaurants, and a lively social scene; good for foodies, digital nomads, and anyone wanting Bengaluru's modern, entrepreneurial energy.
The eastern IT corridor built around tech parks (ITPL), malls, and business hotels; convenient for tech-sector visitors and conventions but a long, traffic-heavy ride from the historic center.

Leafy, traditional South Bengaluru around the Bull Temple, Bugle Rock, and Gandhi Bazaar market, with old filter-coffee joints and heritage streets; calm, local, and authentic, ideal for a relaxed, less touristy stay.
lodging: Sheraton Grand Bengaluru Whitefield Hotel & Convention Center
La Marvella, A Sarovar Premiere Hotel

water.note: Tap water is not safe for visitors; use bottled or filtered water, including for brushing teeth.

transit.hours: Namma Metro runs roughly 5:00 AM to 11:00 PM; BMTC city buses run from early morning to around 11:00 PM with limited late-night services.
transit.note: Namma Metro is the fast, air-conditioned way across the city — the Purple Line (east-west) and Green Line (north-south) form the core, with the newer Yellow Line (RV Road-Bommasandra) added in 2025 and the airport-bound Blue Line opening in phases from late 2026. BMTC runs the extensive city bus network.
transit.pay: Metro uses QR tickets, contactless bank cards, and a reloadable smart card; BMTC buses take cash or the transit card. Auto-rickshaws and app-cabs (Uber/Ola/Rapido) fill the gaps.

transit.m: Vayu Vajra (BMTC) AC airport bus to major city hubs (~60-90 min)
Prepaid or app taxi (Uber/Ola) to city center (60-90 min, traffic-dependent)

tip.r: Not mandatory; many restaurants add a 5-10% service charge, and if not, rounding up or leaving 5-10% for good service is appreciated. Small tips to auto drivers and hotel staff are customary.

food.name: Masala dosa
food.desc: Bengaluru's version is thick, ghee-soaked and slightly sweet, wrapped around potato saagu and eaten with coconut chutney. No sambar at the purist places.

places.name: Vidyarthi Bhavan
places.note: Open since 1943 and still the benchmark; ghee-drenched masala dosa and saagu dosa, cash queues out the door.

places.name: Mavalli Tiffin Rooms (MTR)
places.note: Serving since 1924; famously precise dosas, rava idli and a set breakfast worth queuing for.

places.name: Airlines Hotel
places.note: Butter masala dosa eaten under banyan trees at a drive-in going since the late 1960s.

food.name: Benne dosa
food.desc: The Davanagere style adopted by Bengaluru: small, lacy dosas cooked in an indecent amount of white butter, crisp outside, soft within.

places.name: Central Tiffin Room (Shri Sagar)
places.note: Open since the 1920s and widely called the city's best benne masala dose.

places.name: Davanagere Benne Dose outlets
places.note: Small specialist counters cooking benne dose on cast iron to order; cheap and fast.

places.name: Airlines Hotel
places.note: Butter-heavy dosa with strong filter coffee, best at breakfast before the traffic builds.

food.name: Idli and vada at a darshini
food.desc: Stand-up self-service tiffin rooms serving steamed idli, crisp medu vada, khara bath and chutney from dawn. Pay at the counter, eat at the ledge.

places.name: Brahmin's Coffee Bar
places.note: Legendary tiny counter; idli-vada with famous chutney and filter coffee, closes early afternoon.

places.name: Veena Stores
places.note: Morning-only institution where the queue for idli and kharabath runs down the street.

places.name: SLV (Sri Laxmi Venkateshwara)
places.note: Classic darshini chain for a quick, reliable idli-vada plate at any hour.

food.name: Bisi bele bath
food.desc: Karnataka's great one-pot rice: rice, toor dal and vegetables cooked with tamarind and a roasted spice blend, finished with ghee and crunchy boondi.

places.name: Mavalli Tiffin Rooms (MTR)
places.note: The version most Bengalureans measure others against; comes with ghee and boondi.

places.name: Halli Mane
places.note: Rustic Karnataka-village-themed tiffin room with a deep menu of traditional rice dishes.

places.name: New Krishna Bhavan
places.note: Old-school vegetarian hotel doing bisi bele bath and rava idli well at low prices.

food.name: Donne biryani
food.desc: Bengaluru's own biryani: short-grain seeraga samba rice with mutton or chicken, green masala and mint, served in a dried-leaf donne bowl.

places.name: Shivaji Military Hotel
places.note: The classic military hotel for donne biryani; sells out by early afternoon, cash only.

places.name: Ranganna Military Hotel
places.note: Another old-guard mutton specialist; go early and order the boti or ragi mudde too.

places.name: Hotel Hanumanthu
places.note: Long-running local favourite for donne-style mutton biryani and pepper chicken.

food.name: Chow chow bath
food.desc: One plate, two halves: savoury khara bath semolina upma beside sweet saffron kesari bath. The Bengaluru breakfast compromise.

places.name: Vidyarthi Bhavan
places.note: Chow chow bath alongside the famous dosa; go mid-morning on a weekday to avoid the wait.

places.name: Central Tiffin Room (Shri Sagar)
places.note: Reliable khara and kesari bath pairing to follow the benne dose.

places.name: Veena Stores
places.note: Khara bath from the morning counter, eaten standing with a tumbler of coffee.

food.name: Filter kaapi
food.desc: Chicory-blended South Indian coffee brewed by drip, mixed with hot milk and pulled between tumbler and dabarah. Order it by-two to share.

places.name: Brahmin's Coffee Bar
places.note: Small strong kaapi that regulars swear by, taken standing after the idli-vada.

places.name: Vidyarthi Bhavan
places.note: Classic tumbler-and-dabarah service; the coffee is as much the point as the dosa.

places.name: Indian Coffee House
places.note: Faded, waiter-served coffee house from another era; cheap kaapi and toast.

food.name: Bengaluru craft beer
food.desc: India's craft beer capital: house-brewed wheat beers, hoppy ales and toddy-inspired brews poured fresh in microbreweries across Indiranagar and Whitefield.

places.name: Toit
places.note: The city's landmark brewpub; expect a wait for a table on weekends.

places.name: Arbor Brewing Company
places.note: Consistently well-made ales in a relaxed central taproom with decent food.

places.name: Windmills Craftworks
places.note: Brewery, library and live jazz venue; more polished and good for a long evening.

landmarks: Vidhana Soudha

This monumental granite seat of Karnataka's state legislature, built in a distinctive neo-Dravidian style, is one of Bengaluru's most photographed government buildings, especially when illuminated at night.
Lalbagh Botanical Garden
A sprawling 240-acre botanical garden centered on a Victorian-era Glass House modeled after London's Crystal Palace, famous for its flower shows and ancient rock formations.
Bangalore Palace
A Tudor-style palace with fortified towers and turreted battlements inspired by England's Windsor Castle, offering a grand, fairy-tale backdrop rare in South India.
Cubbon Park
A vast green expanse in the heart of the city dotted with colonial-era statues, red-gravel walking paths, and the striking red Attara Kacheri High Court building at its edge.
ISKCON Temple Bangalore
A modern temple complex with gleaming gold-capped towers dedicated to Krishna, blending contemporary architecture with traditional Hindu temple design on a hilltop setting.
Bull Temple (Dodda Basavana Gudi)
A 16th-century Dravidian-style temple built around a massive monolithic granite statue of Nandi the bull, one of the largest of its kind in the world.
Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace
An ornate wooden Indo-Islamic palace with intricately carved balconies and floral motifs, once the summer retreat of the 18th-century ruler of Mysore.
St. Mary's Basilica
One of the oldest and most revered churches in Bengaluru, notable for its Gothic architecture and status as a Minor Basilica, drawing pilgrims and photographers alike.
Nandi Hills
A scenic hill station just outside the city famous for spectacular sunrise views over rolling misty hills and ancient fort ruins.
Karnataka High Court (Attara Kacheri)
A striking red-and-white colonial-era building facing Cubbon Park, one of Bengaluru's most elegant examples of British-era architecture.

train.note: No international trains. KSR Bengaluru City Junction is the main terminus, with Yesvantpur and the newer Sir M. Visvesvaraya Terminal in the east taking a growing share of departures - check which one your train uses, as they are far apart. Book on IRCTC 60 days ahead; the Vande Bharat services to Chennai and Mysuru and the overnight trains to Goa and Hyderabad sell out fast.

bus.note: No international coaches. The Kempegowda (Majestic) bus station beside the railway terminus is the hub for KSRTC (https://ksrtc.karnataka.gov.in/) services across Karnataka, and private AC sleeper coaches to Chennai, Hyderabad, Goa and Mumbai leave from Anand Rao Circle and Madiwala - book through redBus (https://www.redbus.in/), which was founded in this city. Overnight Volvo sleepers to Goa take about 12 hours.

ferry.note: Bengaluru is 900 m up on the Deccan plateau and roughly 300 km from the sea, so there are no ferries of any kind. The nearest coastal boat services are at Mangaluru and along the Karnataka coast.

half.name: Ramanagara
half.blurb: A landscape of granite boulder hills southwest of the city, a popular rock-climbing spot and filming location for the classic film Sholay.

half.name: Bannerghatta National Park
half.blurb: A forested park with a zoo, butterfly park, and safari zone for lions and tigers, on the city's southern edge.

full.name: Mysuru
full.blurb: A former royal capital with the ornate Mysore Palace, illuminated on weekend evenings, and a hilltop temple overlooking the city.

full.name: Shivanasamudra Falls
full.blurb: A set of twin waterfalls where the Kaveri River splits and drops over a rocky escarpment, among Karnataka's largest falls.
